FreeQrly vs QR Code Monkey: same free static codes, plus dynamic.

For a one-off static code, both tools are free forever. QR Code Monkey stops there: its free tool makes static codes only, with no editing and no scan statistics. FreeQrly — freeqrly.com keeps static codes free with no sign-up and no watermark, and adds free dynamic codes with editing and statistics, batch mode, a barcode generator, and a QR API.
Pick FreeQrly if you want anything beyond a fixed code: editing after printing, scan counts, batch runs, barcodes, or an API — while keeping static codes free with no account.

Pick QR Code Monkey if you only ever need fixed codes and you care most about print design depth: EPS and PDF vectors, templates, gradients, and a 30% logo area. For that one job, it is the best free tool we checked — FreeQrly does not beat it on vector formats.

Is QR Code Monkey really free?
Yes, for static codes: 100% free, including commercial use, with no expiry. The catch is only that the codes are static — you cannot edit them or track scans.
Can I edit a Monkey code after printing?

No. Monkey's own pages say the only limitation of its static codes is that you cannot change the content once printed. For editing and statistics, Monkey points you to its PRO upsell. FreeQrly's free dynamic codes are editable after printing with scan statistics.
Which has better design and download options?

Monkey's are genuinely good: logo upload, colors, shapes, templates, and PNG, SVG, PDF, and EPS downloads, with up to 30% error correction for a centered logo. FreeQrly offers logo upload, colors, and PNG and SVG downloads. If print-vector depth is your whole job, Monkey wins that row; if you also need editable codes, FreeQrly covers both.
Do I need an account on either for static codes?
No. Monkey's generator works without an account, and FreeQrly static codes need no sign-up. You only sign in when you want dynamic codes, statistics, or a dashboard.
